bio.en: Amjad Masad is the co-founder of Replit, an AI-powered platform for building and shipping software with over 34 million users, on a mission to make creating software dramatically easier.
bio.zh: Amjad Masad 是 Replit 的联合创始人，这是一个拥有超 3400 万用户的 AI 软件开发与部署平台，使命是让创建软件变得容易得多。

summary.en: Amjad demos what Replit can do today—letting anyone build and ship software, including full startups, with minimal technical skill—which he argues will blow people's minds. He predicts the bottleneck shifts from making things to generating ideas, and imagines a future where someone runs a billion-dollar company with zero employees. The conversation explores the profound implications for the future of product development, product management, and founders as AI lowers the cost of building.
summary.zh: Amjad 演示了 Replit 今天的能力——让任何人都能用极少的技术技能构建并发布软件（包括完整的创业项目），他认为这会让人大开眼界。他预测瓶颈将从“做出来”转向“想出来”，并想象未来有人用零员工运营一家十亿美元公司。对话深入探讨了 AI 降低构建成本后，对产品开发、产品管理和创始人的深远影响。

turns.speaker: Amjad Masad
turns.en: The idea behind Replit is that making software today is very difficult. We want to make it easier. People view this as a developer in their pocket essentially. We have 34 million users globally. There's people everywhere learning to code on Replit, building startups, building personal software, personal tools.
turns.zh: Replit 背后的想法是今天做软件非常难。我们想让它更容易。大家基本把它看作口袋里的开发者。我们全球有 3400 万用户。到处都有人在 Replit 上学编程、建创业公司、建个人软件、个人工具。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: For people building products, say, product managers, founders, what skills do you see will matter more, matter less?

turns.speaker: Amjad Masad
turns.en: Typically, you're bottlenecked where your ideas are not fitting in because they need to be made and they need to be made quickly. Now, you open up that bottleneck. So now actually making things is a lot easier. Actually, you become limited by how fast you can generate ideas.
turns.zh: 通常你的瓶颈是你的 idea 没法 fit 进因为它们需要被做出来、需要快速做。现在你打开那个瓶颈。现在做东西容易多了。其实你被你能多快产生 idea 限制。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I think people are unaware of just how far things have gone.
turns.zh: 我觉得大家没意识到事情已经走了多远。

turns.speaker: Amjad Masad
turns.en: I could imagine whatever five years from now, someone running a billion-dollar company with zero employees where it's like the support is handled by AI, the development is handled by AI, and you're just building and creating this thing.
turns.zh: 我能想象五年后有人零员工运行十亿美元公司，客服由 AI 处理、开发由 AI 处理、你就是 build 和创造这个东西。

turns.speaker: Amjad Masad
turns.en: The idea behind Replit is that making software today is very difficult and we want to make it easier. And then the layer on top of that is the editor and the infrastructure that runs the editor, including what I described as the multiplayer editor. (00:31:33): And then we expose all of that infrastructure to the AI. And there's almost like a new discipline called AI Computer interfaces. So sort of like HCI is now a ACI and turns out LLMs need interfaces that are actually quite different than humans. They're trying to make them use human interfaces like Anthropic's computer use, but those are really expensive and you need to process all this images and video. So instead, for the shell for example, we give it sort of a text representation of what the shell is doing at a certain increments for package installation. We give it a certain tool for editing. We give it an editor tool that when it's writing the code, it's getting feedback on whether there are errors or not, similar to what a human sees, but it's actually old text just to make it easier. So that's AI computer interface, and obviously, all of that is sitting on foundation models. So the improvement in foundation models has allowed us to build this. (00:32:51): The most important model that we use is the Sonnet model from Claude, from Anthropic, and it is the best model at coding. So that's the model we use for coding, but we use models from OpenAI as well because a multi-agent system. And so we have models that are critiquing. We have manager editor model, and we have a critique model and different models will have different powers. We also train some of our models, like the embedding model for search is something we trained internally. So I actually wrote about it back in '22. I said it's going to be society of models, like products will be made of a lot of different models, and it's quite a heavy engineering project.
turns.zh: 对，当然。首先是我们建的所有 abstraction。Replit 运作方式最底层是 runtime。操作系统、包管理器、语言 runtime。我们建了一个能在任何语言装包的系统包括 native 包。所以 AI 任何时候需要包我可以这里展示一个。顺便 AI 也能截图所以它检查 work。这里你能看到它在截图确保首页在 render。这里你能看它要个 drag and drop library 就装了那个。所以它能访问所有语言所有包包括 Linux 那些所有。然后上面那层是编辑器和运行编辑器的基础设施包括我描述的 multiplayer 编辑器。(00:31:33)：然后我们把所有那个基础设施 expose 给 AI。几乎有个新学科叫 AI Computer Interface。所以 HCI 现在是 ACI，turns out LLM 需要的界面和人类很不同。他们在试让它们用人类界面如 Anthropic 的 computer use，但那些很贵、需要处理所有图像和视频。所以相反，比如 shell 我们给它文本表示 shell 在特定增量做什么。包装安装给它特定工具。编辑给它编辑器工具当写代码时得到是否有错误的 feedback 类似人看到的但其实是纯文本让它更容易。所以那是 AI computer interface，显然所有那个坐在基础模型上。基础模型改进让我们能建这个。(00:32:51)：我们用的最重要模型是 Claude 的 Sonnet 模型 from Anthropic，它是最好编程……

And also assuming that person has time, because a lot of times, your engineers are kind of stuck building the current thing. They're not thinking about the future thing. And so what gets me excited is a lot of these CEOs are building the future concept, the next product they're going to build, the next, say, company they're going to build. (00:41:08): And so it unlocks the creativity and again, sort of unblocks them from that. And look, it's a v1 of the product but it can push things forward. You can touch it, you can feel it, you can say, okay, this really has lags and we should work on it. You give it to your engineers and they can improve on it from there. So that's one persona but I'm really excited about it, the CEO/founder. In companies, one of the things that I think is sort of hard about tech companies is these silos between designers, product managers, and engineers. And everyone feels that pain of, we have low bandwidth communication, which is language and then text on Slack and Zoom calls. And it leads to a lot of frustration, because it's really easy to misinterpret people and again, leads to siloing where people working on something, and then you pass it on to the next team and it's not really what they expect. (00:42:30): That happens a lot between designers and engineers, but the common language that everyone shares is code. Ultimately in software tech companies, everything that we're talking about need to eventually flush out in terms of code. And so what if the language becomes actually working prototypes and working applications? For example, we have a Figma extension that translate Figma mocks into React that runs on Replit. So instead of giving the engineers just mocks or screenshots, whatever, you just say, oh, here's a bunch of React code, just make sure it runs on our infrastructure but don't mess with it, don't move the pixels around. And so I think it just opens up silos of the companies, make communication around product a lot more concrete, because I can give you a working prototype and that'll change how people work, if you can imagine that everyone can make software. It's really kind of a radical reimagining of not just what tech companies are but really what most companies are because everyone can be more general.
turns.zh: 我们看到一个有趣 persona 是 CEO、创业公司 CEO。Tiny 的 Andrew Wilkinson 是大用户。这些人通常是创意人。建了公司、雇了人。很多不会编程。很多是设计师或 PM 或别的。你能想象瓶颈、一堆 idea 在脑里，idea 得通过他们说话 translate。然后别人听他们、假设别人真理解他们说的、然后那个别人去试 build 他们想 build 的。也假设那个人有时间因为很多时候你的工程师在 build 当前的东西。他们没在想未来东西。所以让我兴奋的是很多这些 CEO 在 build 未来概念、下一个要 build 的产品、下一个要建的公司。(00:41:08)：所以它 unlock 创造力、unblock 他们那个。看，是产品 v1 但能推事前进。你能 touch、feel、说 okay 这真有 lag 我们该 work。你给工程师、他们能从那改进。那是一个 persona 但我很兴奋，CEO/创始人。在公司里，我觉得科技公司难的事之一是设计师、PM、工程师之间的 silo。大家都感受那个痛：低带宽沟通是语言、Slack 文字、Zoom。导致很多 frustration 因为很容易误解人、又导致 silo 人在做东西然后传给下一团队不是他们期望的。(00:42:30)：设计师和工程师之间很多那个发生，但大家共享的通用语言是代码。最终在软件……

turns.speaker: Amjad Masad
turns.en: I think a very important scale that's perhaps harder to develop but it's worth working on is being generative, being more generative, being able to generate new ideas quickly, because you can think about it as a factory line. So you have ideas, you have the production of these ideas or the initial production of these ideas, and then you have other people that want to consume these ideas or work with you on these ideas. And so typically you're bottlenecked by the middle part where your ideas are kind of like they're a lot of them and they're not fitting in, because they need to be made and they need to be made quickly. And so now you open up that bottleneck. So now actually making things is a lot easier. Actually, you become limited by how fast you can generate ideas, and I find that true of myself as well. I consider myself quite generative, but now I have this tool and I can build a lot more and explore a lot more and I'm finding that, well, actually, I'm running out of ideas sometimes. (00:45:53): So training that muscle I think is a good thing. I think learning a little bit of coding and not the traditional way of learning coding. If you go to a coding bootcamp, they're going to start with what is Git? Actually my co-founder, Haya, was a designer. When we're first building the Replit together, she went to WebAssembly to do a coding course. And the first day, they spent this whole time on Git and she's like, "What is that? What does it do?" I still don't know what it exactly does, but it's like you're inverting the process, you're giving the tool before the actual problem. And so I think all of that stuff, you don't have to worry about, so things that you don't have to worry about. I think a lot of the, as a PM, as a designer, as someone who's not in your code editor every day, don't worry about all the tooling. (00:47:09): And if you learn a little bit of coding just by talking to an AI, doing a little bit of debugging, building something with Replit, running into a problem and trying to fix it just using AI, you'll learn a bit of coding. And I have this that's been called not by me, dubbed as Amjad's Law, which is the return on investment for learn to code is doubling every six months. And really just learning a little bit of that skill, learning a bit of skill about how to prompt AI, how to read code, and be able to debug it. Every six months, that's netting you more and more power because you're going to be able to create a lot more. It's going to be easier to create. You're going to be able to create a lot more complete things. So that's another skill that I think could be necessary.
turns.zh: 我觉得一个很重要也许更难发展但值得 work 的是 being generative、更 generative、能快速产生新 idea 因为你可以想成流水线。你有 idea、这些 idea 的生产或初始生产、然后有别人想消费这些 idea 或和你 work。通常你被中间部分瓶颈，你的 idea 很多 fit 不进因为它们需要被做、需要快速做。现在你打开那个瓶颈。做东西容易多了。其实你被你能多快产生 idea 限制，我觉得对我自己也是。我挺 generative 但现在有这个工具我能 build 更多、explore 更多、我发现其实我有时 idea 不够。(00:45:53)：所以练那个肌肉我觉得好。我觉得学一点编程不是传统方式。去编程 bootcamp 他们会从什么是 Git 开始。其实我联合创始人 Haya 是设计师。我们最初一起建 Replit 时她去 WebAssembly 上编程课。第一天全花在 Git 上她就「那是什么？做什么？」我仍不确切知道它做什么但你在 invert 过程、在问题前给工具。所以我觉得所有那个你不该担心。作为 PM、设计师、不在代码编辑器每天的人别担心所有工具。(00:47:09)：如果你学一点编程就通过和 AI 说话、做一点 debug、用 Replit 建东西、跑 int……
